problem: The rule as written says the caret always locks the major number. That is true only for major version 1 and above. For a 0.x package npm's caret locks the minor number, so ^0.2.3 allows 0.2.3 up to but not including 0.3.0, and ^0.0.3 allows only 0.0.3. Many published packages are still on 0.x, so a student applying the stated rule to ^0.2.3 would wrongly accept 0.3.0.
fix: Add one sentence: for a package below version 1.0.0, the caret locks the minor number instead of the major — ^0.2.3 means 0.2.3 ≤ version < 0.3.0, and ^0.0.3 means only 0.0.3. Keep the exam-trap wording as 'for versions 1.0.0 and above, the caret locks the major number'.
